evidence: Gell. 3.14.3: dīmidiātum eum esse dīcere scyphum dēbeō, nōn dīmidium
terms.comment: Varro, as Gellius reports him, teaches that a thing cut in two is dīmidiātus, while the share that is half of it is dīmidium with the genitive: so citreum dīmidiātum, a halved lemon, but dīmidium citreī, half a lemon. Gellius gives Plautus’s dīmidium aurī and dīmidium obsōnī as models (Gell. 3.14.14–15).

phrases.latin: Dīmidium citreī mihi dā; alterum dīmidium servā.
phrases.english: Give me half a lemon; keep the other half.

phrases.latin: dīmidiātum eum esse dīcere scyphum dēbeō, nōn dīmidium
phrases.english: I ought to call the cup halved, not half
